questions.subject: bio

It is always both DNA and RNA

All viruses share the same capsid gene

bio-sl.topic: Data handling: statistical tests and graphs in biology

options: Testing whether the means of two samples differ significantly
Measuring the strength of a correlation
Drawing a line of best fit
questions.answer: Testing whether the means of two samples differ significantly
questions.hint: It compares two groups.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the null hypothesis in a t-test comparing two samples?
options: There is no significant difference between the means
The data are not normally distributed
questions.answer: There is no significant difference between the means
questions.hint: 'Null' suggests nothing is happening.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which significance level is most commonly used in biology?
questions.hint: It corresponds to 5%.

questions.subject: bio

questions.subject: bio

options: Reject the null hypothesis: the difference is significant
Accept the null hypothesis: the difference is not significant
questions.answer: Reject the null hypothesis: the difference is significant
questions.hint: Compare the calculated value with the critical value.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: If the error bars (standard deviation) of two means overlap a lot, this suggests that…
options: the difference between the means is probably not significant
questions.answer: the difference between the means is probably not significant

questions.subject: bio

questions.hint: Limit the quantity each user can take.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Why are public goods an example of market failure?
options: The market under-provides or fails to provide them
questions.answer: The market under-provides or fails to provide them
questions.hint: Firms cannot make profit from them.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Sustainability means:
options: meeting present needs without harming future generations' ability to meet theirs
using resources as fast as possible
questions.answer: meeting present needs without harming future generations' ability to meet theirs
questions.hint: Think about the long term.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Why can it be hard for countries to agree on reducing pollution?
options: Each country may hope others cut emissions while it free rides
There are no costs to cutting emissions
questions.answer: Each country may hope others cut emissions while it free rides
questions.hint: The free-rider problem also applies to nations.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain why a private firm would not provide a lighthouse.
questions.hint: Think about who could be charged and whether non-payers can be excluded.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of using quotas to protect a fishery.
questions.hint: Consider conservation versus enforcement and jobs.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain how local communities might manage a shared resource such as a village forest sustainably.
questions.hint: Think about agreed rules, monitoring and penalties.

en-hl.topic: Global issues for the individual oral — HL: introducing the HL essay

questions.subject: en
questions.q: How many fields of inquiry are there in IB English A: Language and Literature?
questions.hint: The topic description tells you.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is one of the IB fields of inquiry?
questions.hint: They are broad global areas.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is NOT one of the five fields of inquiry?
questions.hint: The other three appear in the IB guide.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Complete the field of inquiry: 'Science, technology and the ___'.
questions.hint: Think of climate and nature.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A global issue for the individual oral must be:
options: significant on a wide scale, transnational, and felt in everyday local contexts
questions.answer: significant on a wide scale, transnational, and felt in everyday local contexts
questions.hint: The IB lists three criteria.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: How many texts does the individual oral examine?
questions.hint: One literary and one non-literary.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In Language and Literature, the individual oral pairs:
options: one literary text and one non-literary body of work
two novels by the same author
a film and a song lyric only
questions.answer: one literary text and one non-literary body of work
questions.hint: One of each.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the most focused global issue?
options: The way social media shapes young people's sense of self-worth
questions.answer: The way social media shapes young people's sense of self-worth
questions.hint: A single word is a concept, not an issue.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: How long is the individual oral (before teacher questions)?
questions.hint: It is followed by 5 minutes of teacher questions.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: The HL essay is a formal essay of about:
questions.hint: It is shorter than the Extended Essay.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: The HL essay should develop:
options: a line of inquiry about a studied text or body of work
questions.answer: a line of inquiry about a studied text or body of work
questions.hint: It is analytical, not creative.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What phrase does the IB use for the focused question or angle explored in the HL essay?
questions.hint: It guides the whole essay.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the strongest line of inquiry for an HL essay?
options: How does the writer use fragmented narration to present the instability of memory?
questions.answer: How does the writer use fragmented narration to present the instability of memory?
questions.hint: Look for technique + meaning.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Formulate a focused global issue under the field 'Politics, power and justice' and explain why it meets the IB criteria.
questions.hint: Make it specific, transnational and visible in local everyday life.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain how a literary text and a non-literary text could be linked through a single global issue in the individual oral.
questions.hint: Think of how both texts present the same issue through different conventions.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Propose a line of inquiry for an HL essay on a novel you have studied and justify why it allows sustained analysis.
questions.hint: Combine a technique or convention with a broader idea.

en-sl.topic: Global issues: identifying a global issue for the individual oral

questions.subject: en
questions.q: How many fields of inquiry does the IB English A course use?
questions.hint: Count them in the course guide.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is a field of inquiry?
questions.hint: They are broad areas of human concern.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Complete the field of inquiry: 'Culture, ___ and community'.
questions.hint: Who we are as individuals and groups.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Complete the field of inquiry: 'Art, creativity and the ___'.
questions.hint: What lets us picture new things?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which field of inquiry best fits a global issue about unequal access to schooling?
questions.hint: Schooling is a type of education.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is a global issue?
options: An issue with wide significance that crosses borders and appears in everyday local life
questions.answer: An issue with wide significance that crosses borders and appears in everyday local life
questions.hint: Think: wide-scale, transnational, local impact.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the better-formed global issue?
options: How migrants negotiate belonging in a new culture
questions.answer: How migrants negotiate belonging in a new culture
questions.hint: A good issue is specific and arguable.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In the individual oral, you discuss:
options: an extract from a literary text and one from a non-literary text
a film you have chosen freely
questions.answer: an extract from a literary text and one from a non-literary text
questions.hint: Two texts, different types.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a non-literary text?
questions.hint: Non-literary texts include ads, speeches and cartoons.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: How long do you speak in the individual oral before questions?
questions.hint: Then the teacher asks questions for 5 minutes.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which field of inquiry best fits an issue about the impact of plastic waste on oceans?
questions.hint: Plastic waste affects nature.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which statement about linking texts in the oral is true?
options: Both texts should present the same global issue in different ways
The texts must have the same author
The texts must be from the same century
questions.answer: Both texts should present the same global issue in different ways
questions.hint: The issue is the bridge.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which field of inquiry best fits an issue about government censorship of the press?
questions.hint: Who holds power over information?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Formulate a focused global issue under 'Culture, identity and community' and explain why it is a global issue.
questions.hint: Make it specific and show it matters in many places.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose a type of non-literary text (for example an advertisement or a speech) and explain how it might present a global issue.
questions.hint: Think about the text's conventions and its audience.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain why a single word such as 'power' is not a suitable global issue for the individual oral.
questions.hint: Consider focus and how you would build an argument.
